found_values.value: No finite longest stall is shown with the USB console as written. The parts of a stall, and the cases: (a) one flash window a pass: out_store_tick() erases or programs once, and out_store_reclaim() runs only on a pass where the tick did nothing (main.c:1049, :1083); the longest window is one 4 kB sector erase, 400 ms maximum (packaged-part figure, W25Q16JV-DTR revision I tSE; the die's figure is not known). (b) each console write: pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb_out_chars() loops until every byte is written and breaks only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted chunk; the default is 500,000 us and the firmware does not override it. (c) 900 ms for one main-loop pass in which the host accepts a chunk and then stops reading: the 400 ms erase plus one 500 ms blocked printf (main.c:1059-1086). (d) no bound but the message length while the host keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written: every accepted chunk restarts the 500 ms. (e) at boot, up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 sector erases before can_start() (main.c:937-942, out_store.h:122): 800 ms plus prints, counted only if the watchdog is running by then. The status line every 3,000 ms (main.c:598-601, :1089) adds writes in the same pass

found_values.value: At most 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each of D+ and D-, shared by the RP2354B's USB pin, the connector and the protection, with D+ and D- differing by less than 10 %. USB 2.0 section 7.1.6.1: an upstream-facing full-speed port with a detachable cable may have 100 pF (CINUB), 'comprised of up to 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each line at the transceiver and in the connector and an additional 25 pF ... in the transmission line'; 'The difference in capacitance between D+ and D- must be less than 10%'. report.value: 13 errata affect stepping A4 (CHIP_ID.REVISION 0x8): E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E11, E12, E17, E26, E27, E28. None constrains a pin, a pull resistor or an input front end on A4: E9 (increased Bank 0 leakage with the pad input enabled) affects A2 only and is fixed in A3; E3 (QFN-60 GPIO_NSMASK) and E16 (USB_OTP_VDD and OTP reads) are A2 only. Those that constrain a peripheral: RP2350-E5 (DMA): aborting a channel can fire its CHAIN_TO and re-trigger it; workaround: before aborting, clear CH0_CTRL_TRIG.EN of the aborted channel and of any channel it chains to; cited by firmware/iomcu/src/out_ppm.c. RP2350-E8 (DMA): CHAIN_TO may not fire after a zero-length transfer; do not use CHAIN_TO with zero-length transfers. RP2350-E12 (USB), 'RP2350 A2, RP2350 A3, RP2350 A4 (mitigated on A3)': USB status events not reliably registered when clk_sys is equal to or slower than clk_usb; workaround: 'Run clk_sys faster than clk_usb by at least 10% when the peripheral is in use', at least 52.8 MHz with clk_usb at the 48 MHz section 12.7.3.1 requires; reset, suspend and resume signalling is exempt. RP2350-E27 (bus fabric): BUS_PRIORITY bits are mis-wired on the FASTPERI and APB arbiters; no complete fix. RP2350-E2 (SIO): SPINLOCK writes are mirrored at +0x80; fixed by documentation and software. RP2350-E1 (SIO interpolator): OVERF bits broken by right-rotate. RP2350-E11 (XIP cache): clean by set/way modifies the tag of dirty lines; fixed by documentation and software. Core and debug only: E4 (System Bus Access stalls with core 1 in clock-gated sleep), E6 (PMPCFGx RWX transposed), E7 (U-mode does not ignore mstatus.mie). report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down in microseconds from LOAD (24 bits, max 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds', Table 1249), is disabled at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0x0) and pauses while either core is in debug or JTAG accesses the bus (PAUSE_DBG0, PAUSE_DBG1, PAUSE_JTAG reset 1, Table 1248). The image sets no timeout (V4), against the owner's decision that it enables one (2026-09-25). Against the stop deadline: not checked, because V1 is not found. Against the longest legitimate stall (V2): a timeout above 900 ms covers a pass in which the USB host stops reading, and one above 800 ms plus prints covers the boot erases; no timeout covers a host that keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written, because each accepted chunk restarts pico-sdk's 500 ms console timeout (PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, not overridden by the firmware).
